clue.text: Jug for the " fridge "?.

definitions.meaning: jug is slang for prison, and a prison is also called the ...
a refrigerator is something that chills things down

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: slang for a jail, and a domestic appliance that chills food.

clue.text: The Board affirms Franco- German agreements

parts.note: oui is French for yes
ja is German for yes

explanation.surface: The governing body backs treaties between France and Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affirms' is a link; the board is the one used in seances.
explanation.definitionFit: A Ouija board is a lettered board used in seances to receive messages.

clue.text: One of industry's 28 ?

parts.note: 28 across reads as the keymen; a tradesman who makes keys is literally one of them

explanation.walkthrough: 28 across names indispensable staff; this craftsman cuts keys, so he is a key man in a literal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A locksmith makes and repairs locks and keys.

clue.text: Implement for combing a slight wave

definitions.meaning: a toothed comb used to strip seeds from flax

explanation.definitionFit: A flax comb and a small wavelet share one name.

clue.text: If mantle needs repair, try a thread-like fibre

indicators.note: something needing repair must be put back together, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A gas mantle wants mending, so the householder tries a fine thread instead.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal 'needs repair' rearranges IFMANTLE; 'try' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A filament is a very fine strand, like the glowing wire in a lamp.

clue.text: Polish academy nearing completion?

definitions.meaning: a school that polishes young ladies' manners
in the act of finishing, near the end

explanation.definitionFit: A finishing school teaches social graces; read literally, a school that is ending.

clue.text: Featureless way to suffer a setback

definitions.meaning: read literally, to be left without a face, with no features
to be humiliated and lose standing

explanation.definitionFit: To be humiliated is to lose respect; literally it means having no visage.

clue.text: Power, possibly, when May is past

definitions.meaning: the past tense of the verb may

explanation.definitionFit: Might is strength, and also the past form of the verb may.

clue.text: Sure of in a wrong, very wicked way

indicators.note: put in a wrong way means set in a wrong order, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Being certain about something in a mistaken manner is deeply evil.
explanation.definitionFit: Nefarious means villainous, criminal in a flagrant way.

clue.text: Black Forest' trees in America ?

parts.note: read 'Black' as tar-black and 'Forest trees' as conifers, then move them to the New World where this resinous conifer grows

explanation.walkthrough: The Black Forest is in Germany; the clue asks what black forest trees would be in America, where the pitch-black word and the pine trees combine into a native species.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitch pine is a resinous pine native to eastern North America.

clue.text: Present in grog if taken in the right spirit

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words grog if taken, running across them

explanation.surface: A drink of rum is a welcome offering, provided it is received in the proper spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'groG IF Taken'; 'in the right spirit' completes the picture of rum and plays on spirit as alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: A present is something given freely, a donation or offering.

clue.text: Artists back sales of Johnson's book

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist, so artists are RAS

indicators.note: back means the word sales is read from its end to its start

explanation.surface: Painters support the selling of a famous literary work.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Johnson wrote the moral tale Rasselas, Prince of Abissinia (1759). 'back' turns SALES into SELAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Johnson's 1759 prose romance carries this title.

clue.text: "I dipt into the —-, far as human eye could see" (Tennyson)

definitions.text: I dipt into the —-, far as human eye could see" (Tennyson

parts.words: I dipt into the —-, far as human eye could see" (Tennyson
parts.note: a quotation to complete: the missing word is what the poet's eye peers into, the time still to come

explanation.walkthrough: The line is from Tennyson's Locksley Hall: 'For I dipt into the future, far as human eye could see'.
explanation.definitionFit: The poet gazes forward into time yet to come, the coming years.

clue.text: A way one takes wine

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A route someone follows to drink wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine from Piedmont.

clue.text: Galactic disaster merits no tears …

parts.note: the Milky Way pictured as a dairy spillage, and the proverb says not to cry over such a mishap

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'no use crying over spilt milk'; 'Galactic' points to the Milky Way.
explanation.definitionFit: Spilt milk stands for a mishap that cannot be undone, so tears are wasted.

clue.text: Change in coin is responsible for this cut

indicators.note: change here means alter the order of these letters, while the surface means coins

explanation.surface: Loose coins are blamed for a gash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' looks like loose coins beside 'coin'; it rearranges INCOINIS.
explanation.definitionFit: An incision is a cut made with a blade, as by a surgeon.

clue.text: … but perhaps tiny cries show good faith

indicators.note: perhaps marks one possible rearrangement of the letters of tiny cries

explanation.surface: Small sobs may prove that someone is genuine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges TINYCRIES; the clue follows on from 14 down's dots.
explanation.definitionFit: Sincerity is genuineness, honest intent.

clue.text: A machine to tune with skill

parts.note: an air is a tune or melody
craft is skill

explanation.surface: A device for playing melodies with dexterity.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft is a flying machine.

clue.text: Settling by " visible means "?

definitions.meaning: to light on something is to land or settle there, as a bird does
illumination is the means by which things become visible

explanation.definitionFit: Lighting is both alighting, coming down to rest, and the illumination that lets us see.

clue.text: Feature: three quarters empty

parts.note: the compass quarters include N, S and E; here N
O is a zero, an empty ring
the other two of the three compass quarters, S and E

explanation.surface: A characteristic: most of something stands vacant.
explanation.walkthrough: The three quarters are the compass points N, S, E; empty O sits among them.
explanation.definitionFit: A facial feature is a part of the face, such as the organ of smell.

clue.text: This is anti 17

parts.note: 17 down is the flying machine, so this is the gunfire used against it, in old signallers' slang

explanation.walkthrough: In First World War signallers' alphabet A was 'ack', so AA (anti-aircraft) became ack-ack.
explanation.definitionFit: Ack-ack is anti-aircraft fire, from the signallers' name for the letters AA.

clue.text: Debilitated, hence the 'need for this?

definitions.meaning: someone run down needs a pick-me-up, read as two words

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word into 'a tonic', the remedy that a weak person needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Atonic means lacking normal tone or strength, and split it names a restorative drink.

clue.text: Column in flight

parts.note: a flight of stairs, not an aeroplane; the column is the post at its foot or round which it winds

explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' suggests air travel but means a staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: A newel is the central pillar of a spiral staircase or the post at the end of a banister.

clue.text: Tap observed to be crooked

parts.note: a cock is a tap or valve
eyed means watched or observed

explanation.surface: A faucet that was inspected turns out to be bent.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockeyed means askew, not straight.

clue.text: Electronic machine. There's one in the Eagle

indicators.note: in puts the numeral inside the bird's name

parts.note: an erne is a sea eagle
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A computer is found inside a bird of prey.
explanation.walkthrough: ERNIE is the British computer that picks Premium Bond prize numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: ERNIE (Electronic Random Number Indicator Equipment) draws Premium Bond winners in the UK.

clue.text: Adjunct, to a' novel room

parts.note: E. M. Forster's novel title attaches something to a room, and that attachment is wanted

explanation.walkthrough: Forster's novel is A Room with a View; the answer is what the title adds to the room.
explanation.definitionFit: Forster's title gives a room an outlook, the scene seen from its window.

clue.text: Canvas too one adapts for minor occupations

indicators.note: to adapt is to remake something into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone converts canvas for little hobbies.
explanation.definitionFit: Avocations are hobbies, pursuits followed beside one's main work.

clue.text: Like the framework in some: cupboards

definitions.text: Like the framework in some: cupboards

parts.words: Like the framework in some: cupboards
parts.note: the family secret said to be kept in a cupboard is a set of bones, so this is the adjective for such a framework

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is 'a skeleton in the cupboard', a hidden scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Skeletal describes the bony framework of a body.

clue.text: Piano tuners essential to the business ?

definitions.meaning: people who work on the keys of a piano
the staff a firm cannot do without

explanation.definitionFit: Key staff are indispensable workers, and piano technicians work on the keys.
